thread.title: Midland's Aniya Clinton earns All-Big 12 honors as K-State trio recognized
thread.title_full: Midland's Aniya Clinton earns All-Big 12 honors as K-State trio recognized

author: Midland Times
title: Midland's Aniya Clinton earns All-Big 12 honors as K-State trio recognized
text:
Midland native Aniya Clinton has been recognized in the Big 12, earning Second Team All-Big 12 honors as part of Kansas State's achievements in this year's conference awards.
According to a news release, the redshirt junior and former Midland High standout was acknowledged for her performance during the 2025 season. Clinton delivered 17 double-digit kill performances, three 20-kill outings, and consecutive 25-kill matches, establishing herself as one of the Wildcats' key offensive players. She ranked second on the team in kills and points and recorded eight double-doubles, following her recognition on the All-Big 12 Rookie Team in 2023.
The release also noted that Clinton was joined on the All-Big 12 Second Team by senior setter Ava LeGrand. Senior outside hitter Shaylee Myers led K-State’s selections with a unanimous First Team nod. This marked the first instance where all three Wildcats received all-conference distinctions. Myers is close to achieving a milestone of 1,000 career kills and became only the sixth player in program history to receive unanimous First Team honors. These recognitions bring the total to nine All-Big 12 awards under third-year head coach Jason Mansfield.
LeGrand's selection followed a season where she took charge of the Wildcats' offense, leading in assists and service aces. Her tally of 995 assists and 16 double-doubles placed her among the Big 12's top statistical performers, nearly reaching her first 1,000-assist season. Meanwhile, Myers continued her impressive campaign with a record-setting performance that included a single-match program record of 34 kills during the rally-scoring era.
Kansas State (17-9, 10-8 Big 12) will return to the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2021, traveling to Lincoln, Nebraska, to face San Diego in the opening round on December 5. For Clinton—who excelled at Midland High School, earned Texas Girls Coaches Association (TGCA) All-State honors and contributed to multiple postseason appearances—the tournament berth represents another opportunity in her collegiate career that continues to be celebrated by her hometown.
